record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Infinite paths in super-linear preferential attachment with fitness
record.original_question: In super-linear preferential attachment trees with fitness, vertices have i.i.d. weights W_i, a new vertex n attaches to an existing vertex i with probability proportional to f(deg_{n-1}(i), W_i), and f grows super-linearly in degree. The source gives a summability condition for emergence of an infinite star. Is there an analogous general condition, along the same lines, that characterizes emergence of a unique infinite path?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5 Can one identify a more general condition, along the lines of (1), for the emergence of an infinite path?
We consider a model of randomly growing trees called super-linear preferential attachment with fitness

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following randomly growing tree model, called super-linear preferential attachment with fitness. Let $(W_i)_{i\ge 1}$ be a sequence of i.i.d. positive random weights with common distribution $\mu$, and let $f:\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\times(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a function that is strictly increasing and grows super-linearly in its first (degree) argument, i.e. $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} 1/f(k,w) < \infty$ for $\mu$-a.e. $w$. Build a sequence of rooted trees $(T_n)_{n\ge 1}$ as follows: $T_1$ consists of a single root vertex of weight $W_1$. Given $T_{n-1}$ on vertex set $\{1,\dots,n-1\}$, attach vertex $n$ (with weight $W_n$) to an existing vertex $i$ chosen with probability
$$ \mathbb{P}(n\to i\mid T_{n-1}) = \frac{f(\deg_{n-1}(i), W_i)}{\sum_{j=1}^{n-1} f(\deg_{n-1}(j), W_j)}, $$
where $\deg_{n-1}(i)$ is the degree of $i$ in $T_{n-1}$.

It is known that there is an explicit summability-type condition on $f$ and $\mu$ (analogous to the standard super-linear summability condition) which characterizes the almost sure emergence of an infinite star: a single vertex that ultimately receives all but finitely many of the new edges.

Problem. Identify an analogous general condition on $(f,\mu)$ — phrased as an explicit summability or integrability condition of the same flavour — that characterizes the almost sure emergence of a unique infinite path in $T_\infty = \bigcup_n T_n$, i.e. of a unique self-avoiding infinite ray from the root along which all but finitely many vertices have degree exactly $2$ in the path's neighborhood structure.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing emergence of an infinite path in super-linear preferential attachment with fitness via a general summability-type condition (in the spirit of the known condition for infinite stars) is posed as an open problem in recent surveys on stochastic reinforcement models. Existing literature (Oliveira–Spencer, Galashin, and others) treats specific super-linear weight functions without fitness and identifies regimes with finite-degree dominance, but a general explicit characterization for the fitness-weighted model remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Connectivity transitions in networks with super-linear preferential attachment
status_evidence.snippet: For 1+1/k < p < 1+1/(k-1), structure of final tree has a distinguished vertex v with infinitely many children of degree k-1.
status_evidence.claim: Known results address infinite stars/path-like structure only for specific super-linear power weights without fitness.

status_evidence.title: Preferential attachment with fitness: unfolding the condensate
status_evidence.snippet: Preferential attachment models with fitness extend the classical model with i.i.d. vertex fitnesses.
status_evidence.claim: Fitness-weighted preferential attachment is an active research area, but a general infinite-path criterion in the super-linear regime is not established.
